To overcome these challenges, we propose a memory bank-based wavelet filtering and fusion network, which adopts an encoder-decoder structure to effectively extract fine-grained detailed spatial features and integrate high-frequency (HF) information. A long short-term memory bank using cross-attention and memory compression mechanisms is designed to track objects in long video. In extensive benchmark tests conducted on four ultrasound video datasets (two thyroid nodule, the thyroid gland, the heart datasets) compared with the state-of-the-art methods, our method demonstrates marked improvements in segmentation metrics. In particular, our method can more accurately segment small thyroid nodules, demonstrating its effectiveness for cases involving small ultrasound objects in long video. **Keywords:**  Frequency-based fusion; Memory bank; Ultrasound video segmentation; Wavelet transform.

results.content: To overcome these challenges, we propose a memory bank-based wavelet filtering and fusion network, which adopts an encoder-decoder structure to effectively extract fine-grained detailed spatial features and integrate high-frequency (HF) information. In this paper, we propose a memory bank-based wavelet filtering and fusion network (MWNet) to precisely segment lesion regions and target tissues in ultrasound long videos, which adopts an encoder-decoder structure. Although the mainstream ultrasound video segmentation methods primarily focus on temporal information, other approaches are aimed at developing feature extraction and fusion modules based on ultrasound image properties to achieve accurate segmentation. In this work, we propose MWNet to effectively extract multi-scale feature maps in wavelet domain and emphasize the boundary-sensitive HF details, then achieving highly accurate ultrasound video segmentation. The proposed MWConv, memory bank, HFF module can be employed as a generalized backbone and feature fusion module in segmentation tasks, especially for low-quality images and small object in long video.

[# [Literature Review] Tracking spatial temporal details in ultrasound long video via wavelet analysis and memory bank](/file? The paper introduces MWNet, a memory bank-based wavelet filtering and fusion network designed for high-fidelity segmentation of target organs and lesion areas in long medical ultrasound videos. * **Adaptive Wavelet Filter (AWLF/AWHF)**: Input feature maps $Y$ are decomposed into four subbands via 2D-AWT: $Y\_{LL}, Y\_{LH}, Y\_{HL}, Y\_{HH} = \text{AWT}(Y)$ A Channel Attention (CA) module (Squeeze-and-Excitation block) reweights these components, assigning higher weights to HF subbands for high-pass filtering and to LF subbands for low-pass filtering: $Y^F\_{LL}, Y^F\_{LH}, Y^F\_{HL}, Y^F\_{HH} = \text{CA}(Y\_{LL}, Y\_{LH}, Y\_{HL}, Y\_{HH})$ The reweighted subbands are then reconstructed using 2D-IAWT to obtain the filtered feature map $Y^F$.
